newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor seeks JV with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor seeks JV with Russia.

text.p: South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co Ltd is seeking a joint venture with a Russian vehicle manufacturer to secure a foothold in the country, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The spokesman said Hyundai has been negotiating with Russia's largest commercial vehicle manufacturer, named by the official as GAZ, on a venture deal.

"It's too early to say whether we will take over the Russian company or buy stake stake in it," the spokesman said. "We have no further details. But it will take a long time due to the political uncertainty in Russia."
Leading daily Chosun Ilbo said Hyundai Motor, an affiliate of the Hyundai Group, planned to produce its compact car Accent and Avante using the Russian maker's assembly lines.
The spokesman said more details on the Russian joint venture would be available after Hyundai completed a deal with Yugoslav auto manufacturer Zastava, probably in the first half of this year.
A high-level delegation of Hyundai Motor officials are visiting Belgrade for negotiations on the joint venture with Zastava, the spokesman said.
The Yugoslav carmaker is looking for foreign investors to provide capital and to revitalise production and is negotiating with two potential partners.
"As the domestic market becomes saturated, we are eyeing the overseas market. A joint venture is one of our strategies to expand markets abraod," the spokesman said.
He added Hyundai Motor is negotiating a similar deal with other Eastern European and Latin countries, including Brazil, but he gave no further details.
